about: How the equipment families on a job become systems (design §10.1). A plant or multi-equipment group forms when one of its anchors is on the job. Another family joins it only when it shares a schedule sheet, a sequence passage, or a riser or control-diagram sheet with a member; otherwise it stands alone, flagged when a group it could belong to is on the job. Anything not in a group is a system of its own family. Each group's name is a Master Template system name or kind. Edit here, never in code.

sequence_headings.about: Every lettered or numbered heading of the sequence of operation names a system. A heading is a short title ending at a colon or the end of its line: at most max_title_words words (a note in brackets not counted) and max_title_chars characters, with none of the sentence_words, and not one of not_systems. When a section carries an article titled like `article` (SEQUENCES OF OPERATION inside a controls section, numbered or on a line of its own), only the headings under that article count. The level of heading used is the highest one where a title names a bundle. A title names a bundle by its tags, a prefix written in capitals, or its words: the words before any of main_phrase_ends_at, less the generic_words, of which at least half must be in the bundle's kind, other names, schedule title or describing_columns cells (all of them when the title ends in no equipment noun: 'Heat tracing'); when both the title and the bundle end in one of the equipment_nouns, the nouns must agree. A title naming two things joined by 'and', each ending in an equipment noun, is read as two. Edit here, never in code.

order.about: The order of the systems in the proposal, after the front end: the first stage that names a bundle's group or one of its prefixes; anything else comes after, in the order the schedules list it, and existing equipment last.

stages.stage: Split, VRF and computer room units
